transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My mind keeps getting stuck on the same worrying thoughts about what I might have forgotten or done wrong, and I can’t seem to shut them off even when I’m not at school. It has just left me feeling so exhausted and drained lately.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific repetitive actions or mental rituals—like checking things repeatedly or counting—to try to calm these worrying thoughts?

Yes, I do. I find myself constantly rereading emails, rewriting my lesson plans, and checking my parents’ calendars and pill boxes over and over, sometimes for ten or fifteen minutes past when I meant to stop. I feel like if I don't do these things, something terrible will happen and it will be entirely my fault.

Do you also experience repetitive, intrusive thoughts or urges that occur without any physical or mental ritual to neutralize them, or do your obsessions almost always lead to these checking behaviors?

My worrying thoughts almost always lead directly to those checking and rewriting behaviors. I feel this intense urge to do them because I'm terrified that if I don't, something terrible will happen and it will be entirely my fault.
Do you recognize that these fears about something terrible happening are excessive or unreasonable, even if you still feel unable to stop the checking behaviors?
I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. Deep down, I suppose I know it might be a bit too much, but in the moment the fear feels incredibly real and I feel like I absolutely have to do it anyway.
